name: Frog Grass Apple Collector
camera_perspective: Third-person over-the-shoulder camera following the frog player
art_style: Low-poly stylized cartoon with vibrant colors, soft lighting, and simple shapes
controls: WASD or arrow keys to move the frog
level_structure: A single open grassy field with scattered apple collectibles. The frog starts at one edge and can move freely. Apples are placed in a grid-like pattern with some clusters. The goal is to collect all apples; a counter tracks progress. No enemies or time limit.
ui_requirements: Win message when all apples collected

required_assets.prompt: Low-poly stylized 3D frog model with green body, big eyes, sitting pose, suitable for a cartoon game
Low-poly 3D grass ground plane with green grass texture, flat terrain for a field
Low-poly 3D red apple model with a small brown stem, suitable for collectible item

requirements.original_instruction: a 3D game that has a frog as player
requirements.implementation: Create a controllable frog character in 3D. The frog is represented by a 3D model and moves via player input. Implement a third-person controller with WASD movement and camera rotation.
Create a large flat grass ground plane in the 3D scene. The ground uses a green grass material and serves as the playable area.
Place multiple apple collectibles on the grass ground. Each apple is a 3D model with a collider. When the frog touches an apple, it is collected, removed from the scene, and the score increments.

tasks.description: Design the 3D scene layout: place grass ground, define apple spawn positions, set up camera and lighting.
Implement frog player controller: movement, camera follow, and collision detection with apples.
Create grass ground material and apply to a plane mesh.
Create apple collectible prefab with collider and collection script.
Test that frog can move, apples are collected on contact, and score updates correctly.

assumptions: The game is a simple 3D collection experience without enemies or timers.
The frog is controlled with keyboard and mouse on PC.
Apples are placed in a predefined pattern on the grass.
The game ends when all apples are collected, showing a win message.
The grass ground is a flat plane.
The camera is third-person and follows the frog.
limitations: 3D models for frog, grass, and apples are not available in the asset library and no model generation tool is available; therefore, workflow is 'unavailable' for these assets. They must be provided externally or replaced with procedural geometry if allowed.
The game is limited to a single scene and simple mechanics.
